svg.text: K11 Shared rail with two carriages
One beam, two rails, one static belt: the storage carriage and the cell carriage each roll on it with their own motor.
2 × MGN15 rails · 1 static HTD 3M-15 steel-cord belt
each carriage: NEMA 23 + omega pulley set, 4 blocks
box freezer → shelf ≈ 1.9 m in 4–6 s at 0.8 m/s
overlap only over the box shelf X 1880–2350
FRONT VIEW OF THE GALLERY (machine X 0–3600, z 1450–2200)
shared zone over the box shelf

g.text: wet cell (ceiling with a labyrinth slot)

static belt, clamped at both ends: it never moves
Controller admits one carriage at a time over the shelf;
a limit switch on each carriage stopping both drives is the second channel.
OMEGA DRIVE: the motor climbs along a belt that stands still
Drive pulley turns → the carriage walks along the static belt.
A second carriage with its own motor uses the same belt,
so both move independently; no second belt, no long shaft.
Rail butt joints at module borders aligned on a jig [U: K1].

g.text: 1/6 The storage carriage hoists a box out of the fridge throat and drives along the beam towards the cell (≈ 4–6 s).
2/6 Over the box shelf it lowers the box onto a stub carrier, then leaves the shared zone.
3/6 The cell carriage — same beam, same belt, own motor — enters the zone and takes the carrier with the box.
4/6 Both carriages move independently: the cell hand cooks, the storage carriage serves the stores.
5/6 The cell carriage is in the shared zone: the storage carriage stops at the border and waits (interlock).
6/6 Zone free: the storage carriage takes the empty box and returns it to the fridge.
